subject: physics_2
question_text: Give two drawbacks of Rutherford's atomic model?

mark_split.label: It cannot explain the stability of the atom
It cannot explain the line spectrum

verification.note: The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this Physics-II paper the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. The book prints the question as "Give two draw backs of Rutherford's atomic model?"; "draw backs" is set as two words and is written as "drawbacks" here — the wording is unchanged. Physics hand-checked: an electron in a circular orbit is accelerating, so classical electromagnetism requires it to radiate continuously, lose energy and spiral into the nucleus in about 10⁻⁸ s; the radiation given out while the orbit shrinks would change frequency smoothly, giving a continuous spectrum, while real atoms give sharp line spectra.

recall_prompt: Say the two drawbacks: what happens to the orbiting electron, and what kind of spectrum the model predicts.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: It cannot explain stability
lines: An electron moving in a circular orbit is
accelerating, so by classical theory it must
radiate energy all the time. It would lose
energy, spiral in and fall into the nucleus.
The model gives an unstable atom.
steps.margin_note: First mark. Accelerating charge radiates, so the orbit shrinks — the atom is not stable.
steps.why: A charge moving in a circle is accelerating even at constant speed, and classical electromagnetism says an accelerating charge radiates. The orbit would collapse in about 10⁻⁸ s, but atoms last.
common_mistakes: Saying the electron radiates because it is moving. Uniform motion does not radiate; acceleration does.
Stating the drawback without the reason. The mark is for the accelerating electron.

recall.must_convey: That the orbiting electron accelerates, radiates and spirals into the nucleus, so the atom is unstable.
accept: cannot explain stability of the atom

steps.memory_tip: Circle means acceleration; acceleration means radiation; radiation means collapse.

steps.label: It cannot explain line spectra
lines: As the orbit shrinks the frequency of the
emitted radiation would change smoothly, so
the model predicts a continuous spectrum.
Atoms in fact give sharp line spectra.

lines.text: No stable atom · no line spectrum

steps.margin_note: Second mark. Continuous spectrum predicted, line spectrum observed.
steps.why: The spectrum drawback follows from the first: a continuously shrinking orbit gives a continuously changing frequency, which is a continuous band, not the separate sharp lines that are measured.
common_mistakes: Saying the model predicts no spectrum at all. It predicts a continuous one.
Naming only one drawback. The question asks for two.

recall.must_convey: That the model predicts a continuous spectrum while atoms give line spectra.

steps.memory_tip: Shrinking orbit gives every frequency; the real atom gives only a few.

insider_note: Two separate drawbacks are asked for, so write two — stability and the line spectrum — each with its one-line reason.
